pages.title: Verses for anxiety
pages.intro: Worry is something Scripture speaks to gently. These passages invite you to hand your cares to God, to remember how he looks after what he has made, and to find a peace that does not depend on how today looks.

items.note: Pray about everything, with thanks, and God's peace will stand guard over your thoughts.
Peter says you may hand all your worries to God, because you matter to him.
Jesus points to the birds and the wild flowers: if God looks after them, he will look after you. Take each day as it comes.
Luke's version of the same teaching; Jesus asks what good worrying has ever done for anyone's life.
David's advice from a hard season: hand your burden to the LORD, and he will keep you steady.
When troubled thoughts crowd in, the psalmist finds comfort and delight in God.
A prayer asking God to search out your anxious thoughts and lead you on the right road.
Worry weighs a person down and a kind word lifts them up: a reminder to speak gently to someone who is anxious.
A mind that keeps its trust fixed on God is kept in peace.
Martha is anxious and distracted by all her serving; Jesus gently points her to what matters most.
Jesus leaves his own peace with his followers, a peace unlike the world's, and tells them not to let their hearts be troubled.

pages.title: Verses for fear
pages.intro: Fear is a very human thing, and Scripture never scolds anyone for feeling it. These passages remind you who stands beside you when you are afraid, and show people who were frightened and found help in God.

items.note: God tells his frightened people that he is with them, and promises to strengthen them, to help them and to hold them up.
David calls the LORD his light and his safe place, and says that even with an army camped around him, his heart stays calm.
Paul tells young Timothy that God has not made him timid: what God gave him brings strength, love and a disciplined mind.
God tells Joshua, who is stepping into Moses's place, to be strong and brave, because the LORD goes with him wherever he goes.
When fear comes, the psalmist chooses to trust God, and asks what mere mortals can really do to him.
God is a refuge and a help close at hand, so the psalmist stays unafraid even if the earth shakes and mountains slide into the sea.
God says he has bought his people back and knows them by name; in deep water or in fire, he will be with them.
Jesus says God notices every sparrow that falls and has counted the hairs on your head, so you need not be afraid: you matter far more to him.
Paul asks who can win against us when God is on our side, and answers that no trouble, no power and not even death can pull us away from God's love.
Where love is complete, there is no room left for fear. John says fear is tied up with dreading punishment, and God's love moves it out.
God has promised never to leave or abandon his people, so they can say with confidence that the Lord is their helper and they need not be afraid.
The psalmist sought the LORD, was answered and was freed from all his fears; he invites everyone to try for themselves and see that God is good.

pages.title: Verses for peace
pages.intro: Peace in Scripture is more than quiet: it is being at rest with God, with other people and within yourself. These passages describe where that peace comes from, and how it can steady you when life is anything but calm.

items.note: Jesus gives his followers a peace of his own, unlike anything the world offers, and tells them not to be troubled or afraid.
Bring every request to God in prayer, with thanks, and a peace beyond understanding will watch over your heart and mind.
A blessing God told Aaron and his sons to speak over Israel, asking him to keep them, look kindly on them and give them peace.
David can go to bed and sleep untroubled, because the LORD alone makes him safe.
David says the LORD is the source of his people's strength, and that he blesses them with peace.
God keeps in complete peace the person whose mind is fixed on him, because that person trusts him.
Jesus says he spoke to his friends so they could have peace in him; the world will bring trouble, but he has overcome it.
Isaiah promises a child whose names include Prince of Peace, a ruler whose government will rest on his shoulders; Christians read this as pointing to Jesus.
Paul says that being put right with God by faith brings us peace with him, through Jesus, our Lord.
Christ himself is our peace: through the cross he removed the barrier of hostility between Jews and non-Jews, and brought both to God.
Paul asks believers to let the peace Christ gives decide matters in their hearts, as parts of one body, and to be thankful.
Paul asks Christians to do their part, as far as it depends on them, to live in peace with everyone.

pages.title: Verses for hope
pages.intro: In Scripture, hope is not wishful thinking but a confident waiting for something God has promised. These passages come from people in exile, in sorrow and in long waiting, and they offer hope to you as steady ground.

items.note: God tells exiles in Babylon that he has plans for their good and a hopeful future, and that they will find him when they seek him wholeheartedly.
Paul prays that the God of hope will fill believers with joy and peace as they trust him, so that hope overflows by the Spirit's power.
The LORD never grows tired and gives strength to the weary; those who wait on him find their strength renewed and rise up like eagles.
In the middle of grief, the writer recalls that God's love never runs out and his mercies begin afresh each morning, and so chooses to wait for him in hope.
The psalmist speaks to his own sinking spirit and tells it to wait with hope for God, whom he will yet praise.
Waiting for the LORD is like a night watchman waiting for dawn; the psalmist urges Israel to hope in him, since his love and rescue are plentiful.
Paul traces a chain: hardship builds endurance, endurance builds character, character builds hope, and this hope will not let us down because the Spirit has filled our hearts with God's love.
Hope is by nature about things we cannot yet see, Paul says, and so we wait for it patiently.
God's promise and oath cannot be broken, so those who run to him are strongly encouraged; this hope holds the soul steady like an anchor.
Peter praises God, who through Jesus's resurrection gave believers a living hope and an inheritance that cannot spoil or fade, kept safe in heaven for them.
Proverbs admits that a hope that keeps being delayed makes the heart sick, while a longing finally met is like a tree of life.
Hold on firmly to the hope we declare, the writer says, because God, who made the promise, can be trusted.

pages.title: Verses for grief and loss
pages.intro: Grief takes the time it takes, and Scripture does not hurry anyone through it. These passages give mourners words to cry with, show Jesus weeping at a friend's grave, and speak of a God who stays close to the brokenhearted.

items.note: The LORD is close to people whose hearts are broken, and he rescues those who are crushed in spirit.
Even in the darkest valley, the shepherd is with you, and his rod and staff bring comfort.
Jesus calls mourners blessed and promises that comfort is coming to them.
Mary falls at Jesus's feet in tears, and Jesus, deeply moved, weeps with her over the death of his friend Lazarus.
One anointed by the Spirit is sent to mend broken hearts and comfort all who mourn, giving beauty in place of ashes and joy in place of sorrow.
The psalmist asks God to keep his tears in a bottle and trusts that each one is written down: God notices every tear.
An honest cry: the psalmist asks how long God will seem to forget him, with sorrow in his heart every day. Scripture makes room for that kind of asking.
The Teacher observes that life moves through seasons, and that there is a season for tears and for laughter, for grieving and for dancing.
Paul praises God as a compassionate Father and the source of all comfort, who helps us in trouble so that we can help others in theirs.
Paul's simple advice for friends: share in other people's joy, and cry alongside those who are crying.
Paul comforts believers grieving loved ones who have died in Jesus: they grieve, but not without hope, because the Lord's coming will bring everyone together with him.
items.doctrine_note: Christians understand the order, timing and manner of the Lord's coming described here in different ways, including when believers are gathered to him and how this fits with other events.

items.note: John sees God making his home among his people, wiping away all their tears, and ending death, mourning, crying and pain.

pages.title: Verses for forgiveness
pages.intro: Scripture speaks of forgiveness in both directions: God forgiving those who come to him, and his people forgiving one another. These passages are for anyone carrying guilt, and for anyone who is finding it hard to forgive.

items.note: The LORD is kind, patient and rich in love; he does not treat us as our sins deserve, and puts our wrongs as far from us as sunrise is from sunset.
If we own up to our sins, God can be trusted to forgive them and make us clean from every wrong.
A father runs to welcome his lost son home. The story shows how ready God is to forgive; the older brother finds it hard to join the celebration.
In the prayer he teaches, Jesus ties asking God to forgive us to forgiving other people, and then comments on that link.
Asked how often to forgive, Jesus says far more than seven times, then tells of a servant let off a huge debt who would not forgive a small one.
From the cross, Jesus asks his Father to forgive the people who are killing him, because they do not realise what they are doing.
Paul asks believers to drop bitterness, rage and slander, and to be kind and warm-hearted, forgiving one another as God forgave them in Christ.
David writes of the joy of being forgiven, and of how staying silent about his wrong wore him down until he finally admitted it to God.
God invites his people to talk things over, and promises that even sins that stain like crimson dye can be washed white as snow.
Micah marvels at a God who forgives wrongdoing, delights in showing mercy, and casts every sin of ours into the ocean depths.
After Jacob dies, Joseph's frightened brothers beg his forgiveness. He weeps, tells them not to fear, says God turned their evil into good, and speaks kindly to them.
As he is being stoned, Stephen asks the Lord Jesus to receive his spirit and not to hold this sin against the people killing him.

pages.title: Verses for healing
pages.intro: The Bible speaks of healing in many ways: God as the one who heals, Jesus healing the sick, and healing among the gifts of the church. Read these gently if you are ill, or caring for someone who is; they say what they say and do not explain every case.

items.note: God tells Israel that if they listen and obey, he will spare them the diseases that struck Egypt, and he calls himself their healer.
David urges himself to remember all the LORD's kindnesses: he forgives every sin and heals every illness.
King Hezekiah, told he will die, prays and weeps; God hears, sees his tears, and promises to heal him and add fifteen years to his life.
The suffering servant carries our sicknesses and sorrows and is pierced for our wrongdoing; through his wounds, healing comes to us.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on whether the healing spoken of here means forgiveness and spiritual restoration, healing of the body, or both.

items.note: In the evening many troubled by spirits are carried to Jesus; he drives the spirits out and heals all the sick; Matthew says this fulfils what Isaiah wrote.
items.doctrine_note: Christians understand Matthew's use of Isaiah's words in different ways, including whether they point to healing of the body, forgiveness of sin, or both.

items.note: A woman bleeding for twelve years, her money gone on doctors, touches Jesus's cloak and is healed; he sends her off in peace, saying her faith made her well.
Peter and John meet a man lame from birth at the temple gate; Peter tells him, in Jesus's name, to walk, and he leaps up praising God.
Jesus says signs will follow believers, including putting hands on the ill so that they get well. Many Bibles note that the oldest manuscripts lack this ending.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on the standing of this ending of Mark and on what its signs mean for the church today.

items.note: Among the gifts the Spirit gives for the good of everyone are gifts of healing; the same Spirit decides who receives which gift.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on how the gifts of healing work in the church today and on whether they continue in the same way.

items.note: A sick person is to call the church's elders, who pray and anoint with oil in the Lord's name; believers are also to be open about failings and pray together.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on what prayer made with faith promises, on the place of anointing with oil, and on why some who are prayed for are not healed.

items.note: Peter says that on the cross Christ took our sins upon himself, so that we could live for what is right, and that his wounds brought healing.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on whether this healing refers to the body, to the soul, or to both.

items.note: Paul asks the Lord three times to take away a painful thorn; the answer is that the Lord's grace is enough and his power shows best in weakness.
items.doctrine_note: Included as part of the whole picture: Paul does not say what the thorn was, and Christians differ on what this passage teaches about suffering and prayer for healing.

pages.doctrine_note: Christians differ on whether and how God heals today, on the place of prayer for the sick, anointing with oil and the gifts of healing, and on why some who are prayed for are not healed; this page lists what the passages say and takes no side.

pages.title: Verses for prayer
pages.intro: Prayer in Scripture is simply speaking with God, in a few words or through a whole night. These passages show how Jesus taught people to pray, why you can come with confidence, and the kinds of things worth bringing to him.

items.note: Jesus says to pray simply and privately, since your Father already knows what you need, and gives a model prayer that begins by honouring God.
Instead of worrying, bring every request to God with thanks, and his peace will guard your heart and mind.
Jesus urges his listeners to keep asking, seeking and knocking, because the Father in heaven gives good things even more readily than earthly parents do.
The LORD is close to everyone who calls on him sincerely; he listens when they call out and helps them.
God invites his people to call on him, promising to answer and to show them great things they do not yet know.
Paul's short instructions: stay joyful, keep praying constantly, and give thanks whatever the circumstances.
Because Jesus our high priest knows what weakness is like, we are urged to come boldly to God's throne to receive mercy and help when we need it.
Jesus tells of a widow who keeps asking an unjust judge until he gives her justice, to show that people should keep praying and not give up.
A proud Pharisee thanks God that he is better than others, while a tax collector simply asks for mercy; Jesus says the humble man went home right with God.
John says we can be confident that God hears whatever we ask in keeping with his will, and that we can know we have what we asked of him.
When we are at a loss how to pray, Paul says the Spirit helps us and pleads for us with sighs that words cannot express, always in line with God's will.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on what the Spirit's wordless pleading means: praying in tongues, an unspoken longing in the believer, or the Spirit's own intercession for believers.

items.note: Jesus gets up before dawn and goes off alone to a quiet place to pray, an example of making time alone with God.

pages.title: Verses for guidance
pages.intro: Many people come to Scripture asking which way to go. These passages speak of a God who guides: through his word, through the advice of wise people, through his Spirit, and by watching over the steps you take.

items.note: Trust the LORD fully rather than relying only on your own understanding; include him in everything you do, and he will straighten your road.
The LORD is the shepherd who provides, gives rest in green pastures and by quiet water, restores the soul and leads along right paths.
In God's own voice, the psalm promises to teach you the road to take, to advise you and to watch over you.
God's word is pictured as a lamp for walking and a light on the path ahead.
God promises that a voice behind you will point out the right way, whichever direction you turn.
James says anyone who needs wisdom can simply ask God, who is a generous giver and does not scold.
We make plans in our hearts, yet the LORD directs where our steps actually fall.
Plans go wrong where there is no advice, but succeed where there are many counsellors.
A prayer to be shown God's ways and led in his truth, from someone who waits on God all day long.
Those who follow the leading of God's Spirit are his children.
Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth, once he arrives, will lead the disciples into the whole truth and tell them what lies ahead.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on whether this promise was given to the apostles only or to all believers, and on how the Spirit guides people today.

items.note: The Holy Spirit holds Paul's team back from some places; then Paul has a night-time vision of a Macedonian pleading for help, and they conclude God is calling them there.
items.doctrine_note: Christians differ on how God guides today, including through visions and inner promptings, and on how such guidance should be tested.

pages.title: Verses for strength and courage
pages.intro: When strength runs low, Scripture points away from our own resources to the God who steadies his people. These passages come from battlefields, prisons and sickrooms, and they speak of a courage that comes from knowing God is near.

items.note: God tells Joshua, about to lead Israel into the land, to be strong and courageous, to keep his word close, and not to be afraid, for God goes with him.
Moses assures Israel, and then Joshua, that the LORD himself goes ahead of them and will never leave them, so they need not be afraid or lose heart.
God is a refuge and strength, always ready to help, so even when mountains shake and seas roar the people who trust him need not be afraid.
Asaph admits that his body and heart may fail, yet he says that God is his strength and his inheritance for ever.
David calls on everyone who loves the LORD to be strong and take heart, because the LORD guards the faithful and deals with the proud.
The LORD gives power to the tired and strength to the weak; even the young stumble, but those who wait on him are renewed and do not give up.
With no harvest and empty stalls, the prophet still rejoices in the LORD, who is his strength and makes him sure-footed like a deer.
Nehemiah tells a grieving people not to mourn but to feast and share, for the joy of the LORD is their strength.
Paul begs to be rid of a thorn, but the Lord answers that his grace is enough, because power shows best in weakness, so Paul boasts in his weaknesses.
From a prison cell Paul says he can face every circumstance, plenty or hunger, because Christ gives him strength.
Paul tells believers to find their strength in the Lord and his great might, and to put on all of God's armor so that they can stand against the devil's schemes.
Paul's short charge to the Corinthians: stay alert, stand firm in the faith, act with courage and strength, and do everything in love.

pages.title: Verses for comfort and loneliness
pages.intro: God is described as near to the brokenhearted and as a father to the lonely. These passages are for the nights when no one seems to understand: they promise that you are not forgotten and that God himself stays with you.

items.note: David says that even in the darkest valley he is not afraid, because the Shepherd is with him and his rod and staff bring comfort.
Feeling lonely and troubled, David asks God to turn to him, to ease the troubles of his heart and to take away his distress and sin.
The LORD hears the cry of the righteous and rescues them; he is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.
God is a father to orphans and defender of widows, and he places the lonely in families and leads prisoners out into freedom.
There is nowhere David could go, whether heaven, the depths, the far sea or the dawn, where God's presence would not still be guiding and holding him.
The LORD heals the brokenhearted and bandages their wounds.
God tells his people not to fear, because he has called them by name and will be with them through water and fire.
Even if a mother could forget her child, God says he will never forget his people; he has engraved them on the palms of his hands.
Jesus invites everyone who is tired and loaded down to come to him for rest, and offers a gentle yoke that is easier to carry.
Jesus promises to send the Spirit to be with his disciples for ever, so he will not leave them like orphans but will come to them.
Paul praises God as the compassionate Father and source of every comfort, who comforts us in trouble so that we can comfort others in theirs.
God has promised never to leave or abandon his people, so they can be content with what they have and say that the Lord is their helper.

pages.title: Verses for trust in God
pages.intro: To trust God is to lean the weight of our lives on him, in plenty and in trouble. These passages come from people who chose trust when things were uncertain, and they show what God does for those who rest on him.

items.note: Some nations rely on chariots and horses, but David's people rely on the LORD their God; the first group collapses, while those who trust him stand firm.
David urges trust in the LORD along with doing good, taking delight in him and committing your way to him, and promises that God will act.
When afraid, David puts his trust in God and asks what mere flesh can do to him.
David tells himself to wait quietly for God, his rock and fortress, and urges the people to trust him at all times and pour out their hearts to him.
Anyone who trusts the LORD is compared to Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, and God surrounds his people as hills surround Jerusalem.
Rely on the LORD with all your heart rather than on your own understanding, and in every path he will make your way straight.
God keeps in perfect peace the person whose mind is fixed on him, so the people are told to trust the LORD for ever, for he is an eternal rock.
The person who trusts the LORD is like a tree planted by water, which does not fear the heat and keeps bearing fruit even in a year of drought.
Facing a furnace, three young men say that God is able to save them, and that even if he does not, they still will not bow to an idol.
Nahum says the LORD is good, a safe refuge when trouble comes, and he cares for everyone who shelters in him.
On the night before his death Jesus tells his troubled friends not to let their hearts be shaken, but to trust in God and in him.
Paul assures believers that, in everything, God is working towards good for those who love him and are called by his purpose.

pages.title: Verses for faith and doubt
pages.intro: Faith is trusting God before we can see the outcome, and the Bible is honest that doubt visits even believers. These passages show faith described, doubt met with patience, and Jesus lifting up people who struggle to believe.

items.note: Faith is described as confidence in what we hope for and certainty about what we cannot see; by it we understand that God made the universe by his word.
Pleasing God is impossible without faith, for whoever draws near to him must believe that he is real and that he rewards those who seek him.
A father whose son is sick tells Jesus he believes, and in the same breath asks Jesus to help his unbelief; Jesus does not turn him away.
Peter steps onto the water at Jesus' word but sinks when he looks at the wind; Jesus catches him at once and asks why he doubted.
Thomas will not believe until he sees Jesus' wounds; Jesus appears, invites him to touch them, and then calls blessed those who believe without seeing.
The apostles ask Jesus to increase their faith, and he answers that faith as small as a mustard seed could uproot a tree.
Paul says that faith comes from hearing the message, and that the message is heard through the word about Christ.
James says anyone lacking wisdom should ask God, who gives generously, but must ask without doubting, for the doubter is tossed like a wave in the wind.
Believers are told to show mercy to those who are doubting, and to rescue others as if pulling them out of a fire.
Paul reminds believers that they live by faith, not by what they can see.
Salvation is God's gift received through faith, not something we earn, so nobody has reason to boast.
In the midst of puzzling events God tells the prophet that the proud are not upright, but the righteous person will live by faithfulness.

pages.title: Verses for joy
pages.intro: Biblical joy is deeper than a good mood; it grows from knowing God, and it can live beside sorrow. These passages celebrate joy in his presence, joy that follows weeping, and joy that no hardship can remove.

items.note: David says God shows him the path of life, and that in his presence is complete joy, with pleasures at his right hand for ever.
God's anger is brief but his favor lasts a lifetime; tears may last through the night, yet joy arrives with the morning.
The psalmist calls everyone to rejoice and be glad in the day that the LORD has made.
Returning exiles laugh and sing for joy at what God has done, and the psalm promises that those who sow with tears will reap with shouts of joy.
God is with his people as a mighty savior; he delights in them, quiets them with his love and rejoices over them with singing.
Jesus tells his followers to remain in his love and obey him, so that his joy may be in them and their joy may be complete.
Jesus compares the disciples' coming grief to a woman in labor, whose pain turns to joy at the birth, and promises a joy that no one can take away.
Paul says God's kingdom is not about food and drink but about righteousness, peace and joy given by the Holy Spirit.
Joy is named among the fruit that the Holy Spirit produces in believers, together with love, peace, patience and self-control.
From prison Paul urges the church to rejoice in the Lord always, and repeats it for emphasis.
Believers love Jesus without having seen him, and they rejoice with a joy too great for words as they receive the salvation of their souls.
James tells believers to count it pure joy when they meet trials, because testing builds the endurance that makes them mature and complete.

pages.title: Verses for thankfulness
pages.intro: Giving thanks turns our eyes from what we lack to what God has done. These passages invite thanks in song, in daily habit and in hard times, and they show how thankfulness is both a command and a delight.

items.note: The psalm calls God's people to sing and shout to the LORD and to come before him with thanksgiving, for he is a great God and King.
All the earth is urged to serve the LORD with gladness, enter his gates with thanks, and bless his name, because he is good and faithful for ever.
David tells his own soul to praise the LORD and not forget his benefits: forgiveness, healing, rescue, love and a renewed youth.
A refrain that God's love lasts for ever follows each reason for thanks, beginning with his goodness and the great wonders he does alone.
David's psalm of thanks says that the LORD is good and that his faithful love endures for ever.
Ten lepers are healed, but only one, a Samaritan, comes back to thank Jesus and praise God, and Jesus notes that the other nine did not return.
Paul tells believers to keep living in Christ, rooted and built up in him and strengthened in the faith, overflowing with thankfulness.
Believers are to let Christ's peace rule, let his word live in them richly, and do everything in the name of Jesus with thanks to God.
Paul urges believers to be filled with the Spirit, singing and making music to the Lord, and always giving thanks to God for everything.
Paul's short instructions: be joyful always, pray continually, and give thanks in every circumstance, because this is what God wants for you in Christ.
Paul ends his talk of giving with thanks to God for his gift beyond words.
Believers are to offer to God, through Jesus, a continual sacrifice of praise, which is the fruit of lips that openly acknowledge his name.

pages.title: Verses for patience and waiting
pages.intro: Waiting is rarely easy, and Scripture does not pretend otherwise. These passages come from people who waited for rescue, for answers and for God's timing, and they say that waiting on him is never wasted.

items.note: David is sure he will see the LORD's goodness in this life, and he tells himself to wait for the LORD, be strong and take heart.
The psalm urges stillness before the LORD and patient waiting, without being upset by those who succeed through wickedness or giving way to anger.
David waited patiently, and the LORD lifted him from a pit of mud and gave him a new song of praise.
The LORD is good to those who hope in him, and it is good to wait quietly for his rescue.
Surrounded by trouble, the prophet chooses to watch for the LORD and wait for the God who saves, confident that God will hear him.
God tells the prophet that the vision waits for its appointed time and will not fail; if it seems slow, wait for it.
Paul says hope that is seen is not hope, so we wait for what we do not yet have with patient endurance.
Believers are urged not to tire of doing good, because in due time they will reap a harvest if they do not give up.
James points to a farmer who waits for the early and late rains, and tells believers to be patient and strengthen their hearts until the Lord comes.
Believers need to persevere so that, having done God's will, they receive what he has promised.
God does not count time as people do, and he is not slow but patient, wanting everyone to come to repentance.
The writer says finishing something beats starting it, and patience is worth more than pride.

pages.title: Verses for discouragement and weariness
pages.intro: Even faithful people grow weary and lose heart, and the Bible shows them honestly. These passages meet the tired and discouraged with food, rest and renewed strength. If the heaviness stays, speak with a pastor and a doctor as well.

items.note: Elijah, worn out and wishing to die, sleeps under a bush; an angel feeds him twice and he walks in the strength of that food for forty days.
The builders say their strength is failing, but Nehemiah arms them, tells them not to fear, and reminds them that the Lord is great and awesome.
The psalmist asks his own soul why it is downcast, and answers himself by choosing to hope in God and praise him again.
David urges the burdened to hand their load to the LORD, who will sustain them and will never let the righteous be shaken.
The traveler looks to the hills and finds that his help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth and never sleeps or tires.
The LORD never grows faint or weary, and he gives strength to the exhausted, so those who wait on him will rise like eagles.
The servant of the LORD is given a trained tongue to know how to sustain the weary with a word.
God promises to refresh the weary and satisfy everyone who is faint.
Paul describes being pressed, perplexed, hunted and struck down, yet never crushed, in despair, abandoned or destroyed.
Though outwardly we waste away, inwardly believers are renewed day by day, and present troubles are small beside the eternal glory they produce.
Do not grow weary of doing good, for the harvest comes at the proper time if we hold on.
Believers are told to run with endurance, looking to Jesus, who endured the cross; considering him keeps us from growing weary and losing heart.

pages.title: Verses for temptation and self-control
pages.intro: Everyone is tempted, and even Jesus was. These passages show where temptation starts, what to do when it comes, and the help that God promises, so that the struggle is faced with courage and not with shame.

items.note: Led into the desert, Jesus is tempted by the devil three times and answers each time with Scripture until the devil leaves and angels serve him.
In Gethsemane Jesus tells his sleepy disciples to keep watch and pray that they will not enter into temptation, and notes that the spirit is eager but the body is weak.
Paul warns the confident to take care not to fall, and promises that God is faithful: he will not let anyone be tested beyond their strength and will provide a way out.
Paul compares the Christian life to an athlete's training: everyone who competes practices self-control, so he disciplines his body to win a prize that lasts.
Blessed is the person who stays firm under testing; temptation does not come from God but from our own desires, which grow into sin and then death.
James tells believers to place themselves under God, stand against the devil so that he runs away, and draw near to God, who will draw near to them.
Jesus, our great high priest, was tempted in every way yet did not sin, so we can come boldly to his throne of grace for mercy and help.
A young person keeps his way pure by living according to God's word; the psalmist stores it in his heart so that he will not sin against God.
A person who has no self-control is like a city whose walls have been broken down.
Paul says to walk by the Spirit and not carry out the desires of the flesh, because the flesh and the Spirit want opposite things.
God's grace has appeared bringing salvation, and it teaches believers to say no to ungodliness and worldly passions and to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives.
Peter urges believers to be alert and sober because the devil prowls like a roaring lion; resist him, standing firm in the faith.

pages.title: Verses for love
pages.intro: The Bible says that God is love and that love is the greatest of all gifts. These passages describe the love God shows, what love looks like among people, and why it matters more than anything else we can do.

items.note: Asked for the greatest commandment, Jesus says to love God with heart, soul and mind, and to love your neighbor like yourself, and that everything in Scripture rests on these two.
God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that anyone who believes in him will not be lost but have life without end.
Jesus gives his disciples a new command to love one another as he has loved them, and says that this love will show everyone that they are his.
God shows his own love for us in that Christ died for us while we were still sinners.
Paul asks what can separate us from Christ's love, and answers that no trouble, power, death or life, present or future, can separate us from God's love in Christ.
Paul describes love as patient and kind, not envious, boastful or rude, not self-seeking or easily angered, rejoicing in truth, and bearing, believing, hoping and enduring all things.
Of faith, hope and love, which will remain, Paul says that the greatest is love.
Paul prays that believers, rooted and grounded in love, will grasp how wide, long, high and deep Christ's love is, a love beyond knowledge.
God's chosen people are to put on compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience, forgive one another, and above all put on love, which binds everything together.
Peter says that above all believers should love one another deeply, because love covers a multitude of sins.
John says love comes from God, and anyone who loves knows God; God showed his love by sending his Son, so we ought to love one another.
Perfect love drives out fear, since fear has to do with punishment; we love because God first loved us.

pages.title: Verses for wisdom
pages.intro: In Scripture, wisdom is not cleverness but knowing God and living in his ways. These passages say where wisdom starts, how to ask for it, and what a wise life looks like, mostly from Proverbs but also from the apostles.

items.note: The fear of the LORD, meaning reverence for him, is where knowledge starts, while fools despise wisdom and instruction.
A son is urged to treasure his father's words, seek wisdom like silver, and cry out for understanding, for the LORD himself gives wisdom.
The person who finds wisdom is blessed, for wisdom is worth more than silver or gold, and her ways are pleasant and lead to peace and life.
A father tells his son to get wisdom and understanding above all, whatever it costs, and not to forget or turn from his words.
Reverence for the LORD is where wisdom begins, and knowing the Holy One brings understanding.
A nation without direction collapses, but where advisers are many it stays safe.
Whoever walks with the wise grows wise, but anyone who befriends fools comes to grief.
When God offers Solomon whatever he asks, the young king asks for an understanding heart to govern the people and tell right from wrong, and God is pleased.
Anyone who lacks wisdom should ask God, who is generous to everyone and never scolds, and it will be given.
True wisdom from above is pure, peace-loving, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruit, unlike the bitter envy and selfish ambition of earthly wisdom.
Paul wants believers to know Christ fully, since all the riches of wisdom and knowledge are stored up in him.
To those God has called, Christ is God's power and wisdom, and the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom.

pages.title: Verses for worship and praise
pages.intro: Worship is giving God the honor he is due, with our voices, our hands and our whole lives. These passages show worship in song, dance and quiet, in a prison and in heaven, and they point to the worship God looks for.

items.note: The psalmist invites the people to sing, shout, kneel and bow before the LORD their Maker, who is a great God and their shepherd.
All the earth is called to sing a new song to the LORD, declare his glory among the nations, and bring an offering to worship him in his splendor.
The psalm summons people to sing a new song, with harps, trumpets and shouts of joy, because the LORD has done marvelous things and won the victory.
Those who serve at night in the LORD's house are told to lift their hands toward the sanctuary and praise him.
The faithful are to sing and rejoice in their Maker, praising his name with dancing, tambourine and harp, for the LORD delights in his people.
The last psalm calls for praise in God's sanctuary, with trumpet, lute, harp, tambourine, strings, flute and cymbals, and for everything that has breath to praise the LORD.
David leaps and dances before the LORD with all his might as the ark of God is brought into Jerusalem with shouting and trumpets.
King Jehoshaphat sends singers ahead of his army to praise the LORD, and as they begin to sing the LORD turns the enemy against itself.
Jesus tells the woman at the well that the Father is looking for people who worship him through the Spirit and in truth.
Paul and Silas, beaten and in prison, pray and sing hymns at midnight while other prisoners listen, and an earthquake opens every door.
In view of God's mercy, Paul urges believers to offer their whole selves as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, which is true worship.
John hears countless angels and every creature in heaven and on earth sing praise to the Lamb who was slain and to the one on the throne.

pages.title: Verses for heaven and eternal life
pages.intro: The Bible's promise is not only that believers live after death but that God will make all things new and live among his people. These passages speak of eternal life as a gift and of the home Christ is preparing.

items.note: Jesus says his sheep hear his voice and follow him, he gives them eternal life, and no one can snatch them out of his hand.
Before raising Lazarus, Jesus declares that he is the resurrection and the life, and that whoever believes in him will live even though they die.
Jesus tells his troubled disciples that there are many rooms in his Father's house, that he is going to prepare a place, and that he will return to take them there.
A dying criminal asks Jesus to remember him, and Jesus promises that today he will be with him in paradise.
Paul contrasts the wages of sin, which is death, with God's free gift of everlasting life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Paul reveals a mystery: at the last trumpet the dead will be raised imperishable and the living changed, and death will be swallowed up in victory through Jesus Christ.
Paul says that when our earthly tent is destroyed God gives an eternal home in heaven, and that to be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord.
Believers' citizenship is in heaven, and from there they await the Savior, who will change our weak bodies so that they resemble his glorious body.
The Lord himself will come down, the dead in Christ will rise first, and then the living will be caught up with them, so they are always with the Lord.
God has given believers new birth into a living hope and an inheritance that cannot perish, spoil or fade, kept in heaven for them.
John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and God living among his people, wiping away every tear, with no more death, mourning, crying or pain.
John sees the river of the water of life, the tree of life, no more curse or night, and God's servants seeing his face and reigning for ever.
